specialty: reproducibility and provenance: does every cited evidence/code path exist in the snapshot AND contain what the prose says it does?
summary: The paper argues that a multiple-choice score should be tested against the construct's best constant, input-blind predictor before any arm-vs-arm comparison, and that this floor is itself an estimator needing calibration against a null the construct can realise. It reports (i) nine construct floors with a legality-aware balanced-null calibration in which only MMLU and BoolQ clear p<1e-5 and MMLU-Pro falls to p=0.083, (ii) a 17-cell MMLU-Pro damaged-arm read-out with the honest aggregate 15/17 at-or-below floor and a symmetric-standard flip of 3/12 vs 1/12, (iii) an off-MMLU replication at 9/85 above floor vs 45/85 above chance, (iv) a stratified permutation null (v2) used to re-judge 27 cells, and (v) an fp32-vs-bf16 control that removes all exact ties without recovering accuracy. On my specialty the picture is mixed in an unusually informative way. Every one of the 17 paths in MANIFEST.json exists and I recomputed the load-bearing quantities from the shipped JSON/CSV rather than trusting them: 1403/12032 = 0.11660571808510638 exactly; gaps +1.661/+0.573 pp and ratios 1.1661x/1.0517x; mean(1/n_opt)=0.11087694718844986 and the 2051/12032 = 17.05% restricted-item count both re-derive from the shipped n_opt histogram; the ten legality-aware expected letter marginals reproduce to 15 digits including E[m_J]=0.082954; the 27-cell BH q-values reproduce exactly (qwen3/k14 q=0.0297, olmo2/keep14 q=0.0663, five Bonferroni survivors at alpha/27=0.001852); the max |boot_p - perm_p| = 0.0371 at llama2/k12 and 0/27 decision disagreements are literally right; the 15/17, 10/12, 12/12, 3/12-point, 1/12-CI, 9/85 and 45/85 counts all recompute from the per-cell CSVs; the fp32 section's McNemar p=0.5702 reproduces exactly from the shipped b=631, c=610 and 2532/14042 = 18.0316%; the tie-convention, length-unit and content-floor tables match E-F/E-H to 5e-6. Most impressively, I reimplemented the legality-aware null from scratch (independent RNG, independent seed, stratified multinomial) and got E[max]=0.113876, q95=0.117188, p=0.0833 against the paper's 0.113873 / 0.117188 / 0.083 -- the flagship correction is genuinely reproducible from the histogram alone. Against that, the artifact has a real provenance hole: the manuscript names at least seven artifacts that are NOT in the snapshot (tcodex_out/EVIDENCE_PACK.md, cited eight times in Table 12 as the resolution target for E-A/E-B/E-D/E-E/E-F/E-H/E-I/E-K; evidence/s2_03_symmetric_inference.json and evidence/s2_02_stratified_ordering.json, named in the shipped claim_evidence_map.tsv as the sole sources for headline claims H-02 and H-04; code/gate_bh_27cell_consistency.py; code/gate_designated_denominator.py; evidence/mmlupro_legality_aware_null_MAIN.json; evidence/e2_single_source_assertion.json). Two of the three shipped checkers cannot run in the snapshot as frozen because of those absences, and the third silently scans zero files. The prose also over-claims the checker's coverage. I recommend acceptance: the scientific content is unusually honest and the numbers I could check are correct, but the artifact needs a completeness pass before it is the auditable object the Reproducibility Statement describes.
strengths: The flagship correction is independently reproducible, not merely internally consistent. I reimplemented the legality-aware balanced null from the n_opt histogram alone (stratified multinomial, my own seed 12345, 200k draws) and obtained E[max]=0.113876, q95=0.117188, p(exact floor 1403)=0.0833, p(rounded floor 1404)=0.07767, against Table 1 / tab_construct_nulls' 0.113873, 0.117188, 0.083, 0.077462. The legality-blind arm also reproduces (my 0.104454 vs shipped 0.104457, p=0.0). This is the strongest reproducibility signal in the artifact: it means the flagship row of Table 1 (PDF p.14) can be recomputed by a reader who has only the histogram, which is printed in the evidence file.

The self-falsification is real and it costs the paper its best row. evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:headline records n_survives_blind=4 -> n_survives_aware=2 and names MMLU-Pro as 'the flagship row'; the abstract, intro bullet 1, Table 1 caption and the A.1.5 appendix all carry the downgrade rather than burying it, and the appendix (PDF p.13-14) states plainly that 'the two surviving constructs are therefore exactly the two whose option count was never in question'. The second, smaller defect (comparing against a 6-dp floor demands 1404 rather than 1403 counts and biases p toward 'survives') is also disclosed and quantified: 0.083 vs 0.078 on MMLU-Pro, 0.691 vs 0.657 on PIQA. Both directions of the fix are reported, including the two ARC rows that move in the authors' favour.

The symmetric-standard concession in Sec. 5.1 (PDF p.7) is the right kind of self-correction and I verified both columns from evidence/mmlu_scale_power/mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.csv: over the 12 damaged non-OLMo letter cells, 10/12 exceed mean(1/n_opt)=0.110877, 12/12 exceed 0.10, 3/12 exceed the floor on the point estimate, and exactly 1/12 (qwen3/k14, p=0.0192) has a CI excluding zero. The paper reports the deflated 3/12-vs-1/12 rather than the flattering 10/12-vs-1/12, and Appendix A.5 adds that under BH or Bonferroni neither reference retains a cell (0/12), with the binomial P(X>=3 | 12, 0.05) = 0.0196 that I reconfirmed.

The multiplicity treatment in Table 7 (PDF p.20) is exact. Recomputing BH step-up q = min_{j>=i} m p_(j)/j with m=27 from the 27 boot_p values in evidence/heal_readout_v2_permutation_null.json reproduces every printed q, including the load-bearing asymmetry the text rests on: the downgrade qwen3/k14 survives at q=0.0297 while the upgrade olmo2/keep14 does not (p=0.0172, rank 7, threshold 7*0.05/27=0.012963, q=0.0663). Six cells have q<=0.05 and five clear Bonferroni at 0.001852, exactly as the caption says. Sec. 5.3 correctly refuses to lean on the non-surviving upgrade.

The v2 collapse-invariance claim is backed by a shipped self-test rather than an assertion: evidence/heal_readout_v2_permutation_null.json:selftest_collapse_invariance lists all ten letters with always_L_acc == acc_hat to full float precision and delta_perm_pp = 0.0, and the n_items column (12032, 12032, 12032, 12011, 11405, ..., 9981) shows the test conditions each letter on the items where it is legal, which is exactly the loophole Sec. 3.2 says it closes.

The audit-the-audit section (Sec. 5.4, PDF p.8-9, Table 9 p.22) is verifiable to the digit. From R7_BOOTSTRAP_P_FIX.md's b=631 / c=610 for keep8 I recomputed the exact two-sided binomial McNemar p = 0.5702 (matches), and 2532/14042 = 18.0316% (matches 18.03%), and (610-631)/14042 = -0.0015 (matches). The illegal p=1.042 is traced to (bs<=0).mean() + (bs>=0).mean() = 1 + P(bs==0) with the base arm's 5.44% atom, and the file reproduces the archived 1.0420 bit-for-bit -- that is a mechanism demonstration, not a plausibility argument.

The A.3 ordering appendix (PDF p.15) does not overstate its own evidence. I verified from E-D that 0/27 cells violate acc_hat <= f_const, that exactly 13 of 27 clear f_const by more than 0.2992 pp (so 'could not have violated it under any prediction vector'), that the tightest cell is llama2/k12 at margin 0.0078 pp, and that 36/12032 = 0.2992 pp. The paper states the ordering as measured-under-a-regularity-condition rather than as a theorem, and even names the n_opt-conditional emitter A,A,B,E,B,E,A,A that attains f_const + 0.299 pp.

The retraction ledger (Table 11, PDF p.23) is a genuine artifact rather than decoration: its 16 rows correspond one-to-one with the C-01..C-16 rows of the shipped evidence/claim_evidence_map.tsv, and the prohibited-numbers row is honoured -- 4.8x, 0.2822, 58/91 and 45.74 each occur exactly once in the .tex sources, only inside that row.
weaknesses: SEVEN NAMED ARTIFACTS ARE ABSENT FROM THE SNAPSHOT, and three of them are the resolution target for headline claims. Table 12 (PDF p.26, manuscript/09_appendix.tex:122-129) is billed as 'the one place where the identifiers become literal paths', yet it resolves E-A, E-B, E-D, E-E, E-F, E-H, E-I and E-K to 'tcodex_out/EVIDENCE_PACK.md' (eight rows), which does not exist here (`find . -iname '*EVIDENCE_PACK*'` returns nothing). Worse, the shipped evidence/claim_evidence_map.tsv gives H-02 ('the floor-vs-chance choice changes published conclusions') the single source evidence/s2_03_symmetric_inference.json and H-04 (the v1>=v2 ordering) the single source evidence/s2_02_stratified_ordering.json -- neither is in the snapshot. So the 3/12-vs-1/12 abstract sentence and the ordering appendix both trace, by the artifact's own map, to files a reviewer cannot open. Also missing: code/gate_bh_27cell_consistency.py (named in tab_v2_full.tex:38 as the emitter of Table 7), code/gate_designated_denominator.py (named in 09a_relocated.tex:24 as the assertion that the declared arm set equals every roll-up's counting set), evidence/mmlupro_legality_aware_null_MAIN.json (named in the E-CAL file's own corroborating_records and required by code/recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py), and evidence/e2_single_source_assertion.json (required by code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py). MANIFEST.json asserts freeze_gate_pass: true and named_artifacts_missing: [], which is true only for the 17 paths the freezer chose to census -- it does not census Table 12's own targets or the TSV's evidence_ids column. The fix costs no experiments: ship the files or replace the identifiers with paths that exist.

TWO OF THE THREE SHIPPED CHECKERS CANNOT RUN IN THE FROZEN TREE, AND THE THIRD SILENTLY PASSES ON ZERO FILES. Run as shipped (cp of the snapshot, `python3 code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py --check-only`), the emitter dies with FileNotFoundError on evidence/e2_single_source_assertion.json (line 163), rc=1; `python3 code/recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py --check-only` dies with FileNotFoundError on evidence/mmlupro_legality_aware_null_MAIN.json (line 360), rc=1. `python3 code/check_prose_vs_evidence.py` exits rc=0 with '[scan] 0 files, 21 targets ... n_checked=0 n_mismatch=0 ... verdict PASS' because prose_files() globs paperC/sections/*.tex and the snapshot ships the .tex under manuscript/ -- i.e. the checker reports PASS while checking nothing, which is the fail-open failure mode the paper elsewhere says it is guarding against. After I symlinked the sections/ layout it does run properly (65 sites, 0 mismatches, 1 uncovered), so the substance is fine; the packaging is not.

THE REPRODUCIBILITY STATEMENT'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS NOT SUPPORTED BY ANYTHING IN THE SNAPSHOT. 10_reproducibility.tex:4-7 (PDF p.11) says 'A checker walks all numerals in the source and requires each to be either an exact match to a value in the evidence set, a correct rounding of one, or a stated difference of two; at the time of writing it reports 610 numerals with none unresolved.' No shipped artifact contains that number or that check: the only checker present is check_prose_vs_evidence.py, whose own output JSON reports n_checked=65 over 21 targets, with min_decimals=3 and a two-tier site rule that deliberately excludes most literals (n_skipped_low_precision_or_unmarked=12). It reads floor_winners_curse_calibration.json (the SUPERSEDED file, line 92), not the legality-aware one. Independently, `grep`-counting decimal literals in manuscript/*.tex gives 655 and all-numerals gives 1258 -- neither is 610, so a reader cannot even reconstruct the denominator. My own attempt at the described check found 43 of 655 decimal literals with no match anywhere in the shipped evidence set at their own precision, including 18.03 (abstract and 05_analysis.tex:51), 2.111 (03_method.tex:23), 4.2264 and 17.05 and 0.9003 (03b_nulls.tex:12/22/33), 14.53/35.20/18.60 (03b_nulls.tex:16), 94.8 (09a_relocated.tex:15), 1.271 and 0.0371 (09_appendix.tex:35), 5.72/5.541/31.7 (07_limitations.tex:10), and all 27 BH q-values in tab_v2_full.tex. Most of these are derivable (I confirmed 18.03 = 2532/14042, 0.0371 and 1.271 and 94.8 and every q from E-D, 17.05 from the histogram, 4.2264 = 0.532164/0.125914, 14.53/35.20/18.60 from E-H), but 'derivable by a reviewer who writes the script' is not what the statement claims, and 0.9003 pp (the split-floor tokenizer move in A.1.3) I could not derive at all: the MMLU-Pro four-tokenizer split spread in the shipped v2 JSON is 0.4681 pp and the MMLU three-family spread in reference_250_content_tokenizer_dependence is 1.5031 pp. Either fix the sentence to describe the checker that exists, or ship the checker that produces 610/0.

THE OFF-MMLU 9/85 AND 45/85 DENOMINATORS ARE NOT RECOMPUTABLE FROM THE SNAPSHOT, unlike every other headline count. The designated set is 5 OLMo-2 arms plus 4 truncation rungs x 3 non-OLMo families x 5 benchmarks = 85 cells (04_experiments.tex:23, A.6). The shipped per-cell evidence (evidence/second_mc_benchmark/gate2_letter_content_nulls.{json,csv}) contains only OLMo-2 arms -- 25 damaged letter cells -- and from those I do reproduce the entire 9-cell numerator exactly (shortgpt16 x 5 at +11.21 to +49.66 all p=0.0001; keep14 x 4 at +6.47 to +18.69 with p<=0.0005; PIQA keep14 at +2.61 n.s.), plus the 0/15 at depth<=12 and the 1 significantly-below cell (arc_easy keep10, -2.69, p=0.029). The remaining 60 cells exist in the snapshot only as POOLED five-task rows (mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:reference_250_pooled, one delta per family-rung over n_pooled=7107), and the paper itself prohibits reading a pooled verdict per benchmark (Table 11 row 9, 07_limitations.tex:15). So '0/60 truncate-only cells at any depth clear a floor', '7/60 significantly below', '52/60 underpowered' and '25/60 read above chance' are unverifiable here; the strings '9/85', '45/85', '0/60', '7/60' and '25/60' appear in no evidence file (only '52/60' appears, and only in prose inside POWER_WALL_VERDICT.md, itself a narrative .md rather than a record). The abstract puts 9/85 vs 45/85 in the second-most-prominent position in the paper. Ship the 60 per-cell rows.

THE PER-STRATUM ARGMAX FIGURES IN A.3 HAVE NO MACHINE-READABLE HOME. 09a_relocated.tex:15 states 'the per-stratum argmax is B, E, B, E for n_opt = 5,6,7,8 (4 of 8 strata, 623 of 12032 items), giving sum_s w_s max_L m_{s,L} = 1439/12032'. The snapshot ships only the GLOBAL gold-letter marginal (mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:letter_null.gold_letter_marginal = A:1403 ... J:945) and the n_opt histogram; no file contains a per-stratum gold marginal, and 1439 appears in the snapshot only as an unrelated substring in R7 and the gate2 files. Neither does the tightest-cell figure '0.085 pp attainable violation' or '94.8% of its weight lies in A-argmax strata'. This is the one place where the ordering caveat -- which the Reproducibility Statement itself flags as load-bearing (10_reproducibility.tex:26-29) -- rests on numbers a reader must take on trust. 52 + 93 + 158 + 320 = 623 does at least confirm the stratum-size arithmetic.

STATED PROTOCOL DISAGREES WITH THE PROTOCOL BLOCK OF THE CITED EVIDENCE FILE. 04_experiments.tex:13 and 10_reproducibility.tex:15 both say 'maximum length 2048 for the cross-family MMLU-Pro runs, with zero truncation asserted per shard in every reported cell'. But evidence/mmlu_scale_power/mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:protocol records max_len: 1536, and the string 'n_trunc' does not occur anywhere in that file, so the asserted-zero-truncation claim is not witnessed by the file the MMLU-Pro table cites (E-B). I was able to establish that the numbers themselves ARE the corrected ones -- all 15 letter accuracies in the v2 CSV equal trunc_fix_before_after.json's `after` (2048) values to six decimals, and that file records old_max_len 1536 -> new_max_len 2048 -- so this is a stale metadata block, not wrong data. But an auditor reading only the cited file would conclude the paper misreports its own max length, and the n_trunc assertion the Statistics paragraph promises is only visible in E-D's per-cell integrity blocks (n_trunc: 0), not in E-B.

THE ARC DIRECTIONALITY SIGMAS IN A.1.5 ARE INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT ACROSS THE THREE PLACES THEY APPEAR. 03b_nulls.tex:37 says the two ARC rows move 'by -0.0025 and -0.0063 in p --- real rather than Monte-Carlo error at roughly -17 and -23 standard errors'. The shipped per-row directionality blocks give dp = -0.001205 (ARC-Easy) and -0.005213 (ARC-Challenge) with dp_sigma = -3.34 and -7.34, and dE_max_sigma = -9.78 and -17.75. The file's own top-level `directionality` string gives a third version: 'dE[max] = -7.8e-5 and -1.2e-4, both about -33 sigma'. So the paper's '-17 and -23' matches none of the three shipped pairs, and the p-deltas it prints (-0.0025 / -0.0063) match the printed p-transitions it also gives (0.140->0.136 = -0.004, 0.453->0.447 = -0.006) only loosely. Nothing scientific turns on it -- I confirmed no verdict moves and the direction (favourable) is correctly disclosed -- but this is exactly the kind of drift the paper's own checker is advertised to prevent, and it sits in the paragraph whose stated purpose is 'a correction that a reader cannot audit for self-service is not a correction'.

THE ARTIFACT LEAKS ITS OWN REVIEW PROCESS INTO THE RELEASED CODE AND EVIDENCE. evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:why, code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py:27, code/recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py:6/482/865 and mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:6090 all attribute the two corrections to 'four of six round_04 blind reviewers (X1/X2/X5/X6)' and to 'round_04 R1-01'. MANIFEST.json:provenance_note likewise discusses round_04 snapshot hashes. Under double-blind submission this is a de-anonymisation surface (it reveals an internal multi-round review pipeline and its labelling scheme) and it is also confusing for an external auditor, who has no round_04. Rewrite as 'independent audit' or move the process history out of the released artifact. I note this as an artifact-hygiene defect, not as a blindness breach against me: nothing in the snapshot told me what to conclude or named a target score.

TABLE 5's CAPTION DESCRIBES A ROW ORDERING THE TABLE DOES NOT HAVE, and one cell is compressed in a way that hides a value the text uses. tab_mmlupro.tex:20 says 'Rows are ordered by retained depth within family', but the Llama-3 block is a single collapsed row 'k14--k8' with ranges 0.111868--0.114694 and p 0.1296--0.6631 (PDF p.18), so the four Llama-3 rungs are not ordered or even individually shown. Since the paper's central organising pattern is depth-monotonicity ('all nine are healed arms retaining at least 14 of 32 layers'), collapsing the one family where the ranges are non-monotone (from the CSV: k14 -0.191, k12 -0.474, k10 -0.465, k8 -0.308 -- k8 is NOT the worst) is the least defensible place to save four lines. The per-cell values are all in the shipped CSV, so this costs no experiments to fix.

MINOR, but worth one line each because both are in the audit trail the paper asks to be judged on: (a) check_prose_vs_evidence.py's own emitted JSON records a provenance_gap for the MMLU content null 0.2845, whose only machine-readable home is OUTSIDE paperC (a proposal-directory file also absent here) -- the paper never mentions this gap in the Reproducibility Statement, though the checker it cites does; (b) the ARC-Challenge character-unit 'credit' value 0.347270 and the OpenBookQA character 'credit' 0.416000 in Table 2 are correct against E-H at full precision (0.34726962..., 0.416) but a literal grep for the printed strings fails, so a naive reader's spot-check of Table 2 will look like a miss on two of its 35 cells.
questions: Will tcodex_out/EVIDENCE_PACK.md, evidence/s2_03_symmetric_inference.json and evidence/s2_02_stratified_ordering.json be in the camera-ready artifact? Table 12 resolves eight of its eleven identifier rows to the first, and the shipped claim_evidence_map.tsv makes the latter two the sole sources for headline claims H-02 and H-04. If they cannot be released, which shipped file should a reviewer open instead for the 3/12-vs-1/12 flip and for the per-stratum argmax?

Where does the '610 numerals with none unresolved' figure come from? check_prose_vs_evidence.py reports n_checked=65 over 21 targets and reads the superseded floor_winners_curse_calibration.json rather than the legality-aware file. Is there a second checker, and if so can it be shipped and pointed at the current E-CAL?

Can the 60 non-OLMo x 5-benchmark per-cell letter rows be released? Without them the abstract's 9/85 and 45/85, and A.6's 0/60, 7/60, 25/60 and 52/60, are the only headline counts in the paper that a reviewer cannot recompute -- and the pooled rows that ARE shipped are ones the paper forbids reading per benchmark.

Is max_len for the reported cross-family MMLU-Pro cells 2048 (as Sec. 4 and the Reproducibility Statement say) or 1536 (as the protocol block of the cited E-B file says)? I believe the data are the 2048 re-run because every v2 letter accuracy equals trunc_fix_before_after.json's `after` value, but please either refresh that protocol block or say in Sec. 4 that E-B's protocol field is stale.

Which of the three shipped ARC directionality figures is the one A.1.5 means: dp_sigma (-3.34, -7.34), dE_max_sigma (-9.78, -17.75), or the file's own narrative '-33 sigma'? The printed '-17 and -23' matches none, and the printed p-deltas (-0.0025, -0.0063) do not match the shipped dp values (-0.001205, -0.005213).

Would the authors consider expanding Table 5's collapsed Llama-3 row to four rows? The four values are already in the shipped CSV and they are the one family whose depth ordering is non-monotone, which is directly relevant to the depth-threshold reading in Sec. 5.1 and the Discussion.
Will the round_04 / X1-X6 reviewer attributions be scrubbed from the released code and evidence before submission?
what_would_change_my_score: To 8: (1) ship or re-point every artifact the manuscript names -- specifically tcodex_out/EVIDENCE_PACK.md (8 rows of Table 12), evidence/s2_03_symmetric_inference.json and evidence/s2_02_stratified_ordering.json (sole sources for H-02 and H-04 in the shipped TSV), code/gate_bh_27cell_consistency.py, code/gate_designated_denominator.py, evidence/mmlupro_legality_aware_null_MAIN.json, evidence/e2_single_source_assertion.json -- and extend the freeze gate to census Table 12's targets and the TSV's evidence_ids column, not just the 17 paths it currently checks; (2) make all three checkers run and fail-closed in the frozen layout (today two exit rc=1 on missing inputs and the third exits rc=0 having scanned 0 files because it globs sections/*.tex while the snapshot ships manuscript/*.tex -- a checker that passes on an empty scan should be an error); (3) either ship the checker that produces '610 numerals, none unresolved' and point it at the legality-aware evidence file, or rewrite 10_reproducibility.tex to describe the 65-site, min_decimals=3 checker that actually exists; (4) release the 60 non-OLMo per-cell off-MMLU rows so 9/85, 45/85, 0/60, 7/60, 25/60 and 52/60 become recomputable, and add the per-stratum gold marginals so A.3's 1439/12032, 0.085 pp and 94.8% become auditable; (5) reconcile max_len 2048 vs the cited file's 1536, reconcile the three conflicting ARC sigma figures, and expand Table 5's collapsed Llama-3 row. All five are packaging and text fixes: they require no new GPU work, and every number I was able to check recomputed correctly, which is why the ceiling is 8 rather than 6. To 10 I would want the general claim itself broadened -- with only MMLU and BoolQ clearing the balanced null and MMLU-Pro at p=0.083 unresolved, the quantitative half of the contribution rests on two fixed-k constructs; that would need new measurement and so is outside this ceiling.
blindness_breach_observed: No breach against me: nothing in the snapshot stated a target score, told me what to conclude, or contained a prior review. I did, however, find review-process leakage INSIDE the released artifact, which I report as an anonymity/hygiene defect rather than a breach of my own blinding: evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:why, code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py:27, code/recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py:6/482/865 and evidence/mmlu_scale_power/mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:6090 attribute the two corrections to 'four of six round_04 blind reviewers (X1/X2/X5/X6)' and 'round_04 R1-01', and MANIFEST.json:provenance_note discusses a round_04 snapshot hash. These told me only that two defects had been externally flagged and fixed -- which the manuscript already states in A.1.5 and A.4 -- and carried no verdict, score or instruction, so they did not steer this review. They should still be removed from the camera-ready artifact.
